{{Short description|Type of equation with integer coefficients}}
{{For|other theorems named after Axel Thue|Thue's theorem (disambiguation)}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''Thue equation''' is a [[Diophantine equation]] of the form

<math display="block">f(x,y) = r,</math>

where <math>f</math> is an [[irreducible polynomial|irreducible]] bivariate [[Algebraic form|homogeneous polynomial]] of degree at least 3 over the [[rational number]]s, and <math>r</math> is a nonzero rational number. It is named after [[Axel Thue]], who in 1909 [[mathematical proof|proved]] that a Thue equation can have only finitely many solutions in [[integer]]s <math>x</math> and <math>y</math>, a result known as '''Thue's theorem'''.<ref>{{cite journal |author=A. Thue |title=Über Annäherungswerte algebraischer Zahlen |journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]] |volume=1909 |issue=135 |pages=284–305 |year=1909 |url=http://resolver.sub.uni-goettingen.de/purl?PPN243919689_0135 |doi=10.1515/crll.1909.135.284|s2cid=125903243 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The Thue equation is [[Effective results in number theory|solvable effectively]]: there is an explicit [[upper and lower bounds|bound]] on the solutions <math>x</math>, <math>y</math> of the form <math>(C_1 r)^{C_2}</math> where constants <math>C_1</math> and <math>C_2</math> depend only on the form <math>f</math>. A stronger result holds: if <math>K</math> is the [[field (mathematics)|field]] generated by the roots of <math>f</math>, then the equation has only finitely many solutions with <math>x</math> and <math>y</math> integers of <math>K</math>, and again these may be effectively determined.<ref>{{cite book | first=Alan | last=Baker | authorlink=Alan Baker (mathematician) | title=Transcendental Number Theory | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | year=1975 | isbn=0-521-20461-5 | page=38 }}</ref>

==Finiteness of solutions and diophantine approximation==
Thue's original proof that the equation named in his honour has finitely many solutions is through the proof of what is now known as [[Thue-Siegel-Roth theorem|Thue's theorem]]: it asserts that for any [[algebraic number]] <math>\alpha</math> having degree <math>d \geq 3</math> and for any <math>\varepsilon > 0 </math> there exists only finitely many [[coprime]] integers <math>p, q</math> with <math> q > 0 </math> such that <math> |\alpha - p/q| < q^{-(d+1+\varepsilon)/2}</math>. Applying this theorem allows one to almost immediately deduce the finiteness of solutions. However, Thue's proof, as well as subsequent improvements by [[Carl Ludwig Siegel|Siegel]], [[Freeman Dyson|Dyson]], and [[Klaus Roth|Roth]] were all ineffective.

==Solution algorithm==
Finding all solutions to a Thue equation can be achieved by a practical algorithm,<ref>{{cite journal |author=N. Tzanakis and B. M. M. de Weger |title=On the practical solution of the Thue equation |journal=[[Journal of Number Theory]] |volume=31 |issue=2 |year=1989 |pages=99–132 |doi=10.1016/0022-314X(89)90014-0|doi-access=free }}</ref> which has been implemented in the following [[computer algebra system]]s:
* in [[PARI/GP]] as functions ''thueinit()'' and ''thue()''.
* in [[Magma (computer algebra system)|Magma]] as functions ''ThueObject()'' and ''ThueSolve()''.
* in [[Mathematica]] through ''Reduce[]''
* in [[Maple (software)|Maple]] through ''ThueSolve()''

==Bounding the number of solutions==

While there are several effective methods to solve Thue equations (including using [[Alan Baker (mathematician)|Baker's method]] and Skolem's ''p''-adic method), these are not able to give the best theoretical bounds on the number of solutions. One may qualify an effective bound <math>C(f,r)</math> of the Thue equation <math>f(x,y) = r</math> by the parameters it depends on, and how "good" the dependence is. 

The best result known today, essentially building on pioneering work of [[Enrico Bombieri|Bombieri]] and [[Wolfgang M. Schmidt|Schmidt]],<ref>{{cite journal |author=E. Bombieri and W. M. Schmidt |title=On Thue's equation |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=88 |issue=2 |year=1987 |pages=69–81 |doi=10.1007/BF01405092|bibcode=1987InMat..88...69B |s2cid=119634267 |doi-access= }}</ref> gives a bound of the shape <math>C(f,r) = C \cdot (\deg f)^{1 + \omega(r)}</math>, where <math>C</math> is an ''absolute constant'' (that is, independent of both <math>f</math> and <math>r</math>) and <math>\omega(\cdot)</math> is the number of distinct [[prime factor]]s of <math>r</math>. The most significant qualitative improvement to the theorem of Bombieri and Schmidt is due to [[Cameron Leigh Stewart|Stewart]],<ref>{{cite journal |author=C.L. Stewart |title=On the number of solutions to polynomial congruences and Thue equations |journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=4 |issue=4 |year=1991 |pages=793–835 |doi=10.2307/2939289|jstor=2939289 |doi-access=free }}</ref> who obtained a bound of the form <math>C(f,r) = C \cdot (\deg f)^{1 + \omega(g)}</math> where <math>g</math> is a divisor of <math>r</math> exceeding <math>|r|^{3/4}</math> in [[absolute value]]. It is [[conjecture]]d that one may take the bound <math>C(f,r) = C(\deg f)</math>; that is, depending only on the ''degree'' of <math>f</math> but not its [[coefficient]]s, and completely independent of the integer <math>r</math> on the right hand side of the equation. 

This is a weaker form of a conjecture of [[Cameron Leigh Stewart|Stewart]], and is a special case of the [[uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points]]. This conjecture has been proven for "small" integers <math>r</math>, where smallness is measured in terms of the [[discriminant]] of the form <math>f</math>, by various authors, including [[Jan-Hendrik Evertse|Evertse]], [[Cameron Leigh Stewart|Stewart]], and [[Shabnam Akhtari|Akhtari]]. Stewart and [[Stanley Yao Xiao|Xiao]] demonstrated a strong form of this conjecture, asserting that the number of solutions is absolutely bounded, holds on average (as <math>r</math> ranges over the interval <math>|r| \leq Z </math> with <math>Z \rightarrow \infty</math>).<ref>{{cite journal |author=C.L. Stewart and Stanley Yao Xiao |title=On the representation of integers by binary forms |journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] |volume=375 |issue=4 |year=2019 |pages=133–163 |doi=10.1007/s00208-019-01855-y|doi-access=free |arxiv=1605.03427 }}</ref>
